description: Probe first. After fz-nml.5, decoding 333 x 世 on run/build still allocates one ProcBin view of the rest per scalar (313 of 679 allocations). The ASCII byte walk was brought down to no allocation per step by fz-sc8.208 (cursor), but a ::utf8 head match still materialises rest as a ProcBin. Probe: count allocations by kind (ProcBin vs others) when walking 333 x 世 with <<_c::utf8, r::binary>> and with <<_c, r::binary>>, on interp, run and build. Prediction: the utf8 walk allocates about one ProcBin per step and the byte walk none. Acceptance: the utf8 walk matches the byte walk (no per-step view), pinned by an allocation fixture in the fz-nml block. The fix extends the cursor representation that fz-sc8.208 gives byte walks to ::utf8 head segments; it does not add a second walk mechanism.
title: Matching <<_c::utf8, rest::binary>> builds no view per step
